data.title: IBA launches integrated QUASAR Penta-Guide QA phantom for advanced radiotherapy
data.description:
Ion Beam Applications SA IBA ( (GB:0GZK) ) has provided an announcement.

Ion Beam Applications’ dosimetry division has introduced the QUASAR Penta-Guide Performance Phantom, a multifunctional quality assurance tool designed for modern radiotherapy departments. The device consolidates more than 25 imaging and machine QA tests into a single setup, cutting down on the number of phantoms, setups and separate analysis tools required in routine clinical operations.

By integrating image-based and machine QA capabilities with dedicated analysis software, the phantom supports 2D and 3D imaging, CBCT-based adaptive workflows and automated reporting with performance trending. IBA positions the product as a way for clinics to standardize QA workflows, reduce procedural variability and document results more consistently, potentially improving treatment safety, efficiency and access to high-quality radiotherapy for patients.

data.title: Frasers Property shareholders weigh Frasers Hospitality portfolio optimisation
data.description:
Frasers Property ( (SG:TQ5) ) has shared an announcement.

Frasers Property Limited convened an extraordinary general meeting in Singapore on 28 August 2026, with its board, management and shareholders present physically and via electronic means, to consider a resolution tied to a proposed optimisation of the Frasers Hospitality Trust portfolio. The meeting was chaired by lead independent director Chin Yoke Choong, with formal procedures for quorum, question submission, and electronic poll voting set out, including the appointment of CitadelCorp Services as scrutineer and the abstention of interested shareholder TCC Assets from voting.

The proposed FHT portfolio optimisation, treated as an interested person transaction, was supported by opinions from an independent financial adviser and reviewed by the audit committee, underscoring governance safeguards for minority investors. Management, led by Group CFO Loo Choo Leong and Frasers Hospitality CEO Eu Chin Fen, presented a framework that classifies hospitality assets into stabilised, potential, non-core and redevelopment categories based on earnings, capital recycling prospects, risk-adjusted returns and growth characteristics, signalling a more active capital management and asset rotation strategy within the group’s hospitality portfolio.

data.title: Tesson to Buy Hong Kong Target, Inject Capital and Add Executive Director
data.description:

Tesson Holdings Ltd. has agreed, through a wholly owned subsidiary, to acquire 100% of a Hong Kong target company for RMB98.4 million, funded by a mix of cash and newly issued shares, and to inject an additional RMB21.6 million in capital. Upon completion, the target will become an indirect wholly owned subsidiary and its restructured operations will be fully consolidated into Tesson’s financial statements, reinforcing the group’s control and expanding its asset base.

The company will also provide an interest-free RMB10 million loan to a related PRC target company or borrower, backed by personal guarantees from individual warrantors, as part of broader financial support arrangements. In tandem, Tesson plans to appoint vendor nominee Mr. Huang Yucheng as an executive director upon deal completion, signaling closer integration of the target’s leadership and potential strategic alignment between existing management and new ownership.

data.title: Xinyi Energy Plans Spin-Off and Shenzhen Listing of Solar Fund
data.description:

Xinyi Energy and its parent Xinyi Solar have announced a possible spin-off involving the disposal of certain solar farm project entities into the XYE New Energy Fund and a proposed listing of that fund on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. The projects involved operate under feed-in-tariff regimes, and after the PRC listing, the target entities will no longer be treated as subsidiaries, with the fund to be managed independently under applicable regulations.

The transaction is expected to unlock the economic value of the solar projects more quickly, generate recurring fee income for Xinyi Energy from operation and management services, and provide regular distributions through its subscription for fund units. data.title: Mech-Mind Robotics Ends IPO Stabilization With No Over-allotment Exercise
data.description:
Mech-Mind Robotics Technologies Co., Ltd. Class H ( (HK:9615) ) has provided an update.

Mech-Mind Robotics Technologies Co., Ltd. has announced the conclusion of the stabilization period for its Hong Kong Global Offering, which ended on 26 September 2026, 30 days after the close of applications for the Hong Kong public tranche. During this period, CLSA Limited, acting as Stabilizing Manager, conducted stabilizing actions including over-allocations and market purchases of H shares to support trading in the newly listed stock.

The Stabilizing Manager over-allocated 3,471,060 H shares in the international offering, equal to about 15% of the initial offer size, and then purchased the same amount of shares in the market at prices ranging from HK$76.10 to HK$101.70 per share. With the end of the stabilization period, the Sponsor-Overall Coordinators chose not to exercise the over-allotment option, meaning no additional H shares will be issued, leaving the company’s post-IPO share capital unchanged and providing clarity for investors on the final size of the equity offering.

data.title: Supreme Court Clears Independent Forensic Audit of Fortis Healthcare
data.description:
Fortis Healthcare Ltd. ( (IN:FORTIS) ) has issued an update.

Fortis Healthcare Ltd. said the Supreme Court of India has disposed of its Special Leave Petition challenging a Delhi High Court order that had directed a forensic audit of the company in connection with the Daiichi Sankyo vs. Singh Brothers dispute. The apex court allowed the audit to proceed but clarified that the High Court’s critical observations about Fortis are tentative and only for the limited purpose of ordering the audit.

The Supreme Court further stated that those observations must not influence either the conduct or outcome of the forensic audit, underscoring that the exercise must be carried out independently. Fortis reiterated that it is not a party to the underlying Daiichi-Singh dispute, is neither a judgment debtor nor a garnishee, and that its current ownership and governance structure were put in place after the Singh brothers exited management and significantly reduced their stake.
